Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), and put $n=N/\sqrt{-g(N,N)}$. Write $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. In a chart $(U,x)$ put $v^a=dx^a(v)$, $v_s=(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ and $|v|_{\mathrm e}=(\sum_{a=0}^3(v^a)^2)^{1/2}$.

**(a) Adapted orthonormal charts.** For every $p\in M$ there are a chart $(U,x)$, $x(p)=0$, a radius $r>0$ with $U=x^{-1}(B_r)$, and $K\ge1$, such that on all of $U$
$$n=\partial_{x^0},\qquad g_{00}\equiv-1,\qquad g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}.$$

**(b) Cone domination.** The chart and radius in (a) can be chosen so every nonzero future causal vector at any point of $U$ satisfies
$$|v_s|\le K v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le K v^0\quad(i=1,2,3),\qquad v^0\ge K^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$

**(c) Curve form.** Every future causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] has strictly increasing time coordinate, and for all $s<t$ in $I$
$$x^0(\gamma(s))<x^0(\gamma(t)),\qquad |x_s(\gamma(t))-x_s(\gamma(s))|\le K\left(x^0(\gamma(t))-x^0(\gamma(s))\right).$$
Consequently every spatial component satisfies the same bound, and the curve image is the graph of a $K$-Lipschitz function into Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ over the interval $x^0(\gamma(I))$.

**(d) Flat minorant cone.** The same chart can be chosen so the constant-coordinate metric $\eta_{16}=-(dx^0)^2+16\sum_i(dx^i)^2$ has every nonzero $\eta_{16}$-causal vector $g$-timelike throughout $U$. If $q,q'\in U$ and $\eta_{16}(x(q')-x(q),x(q')-x(q))<0$, then $q\ll q'$ if $x^0(q')>x^0(q)$, and $q'\ll q$ otherwise.

**(e) General temporal charts: exact compact uniformity.** For any chart $(U',z)$ define its temporal locus
$$P=\{q\in U':\nabla z^0(q)\text{ is past timelike}\}.$$
For every compact set $K_0\subset P$ there is $L\ge1$ such that all nonzero future causal vectors based in $K_0$, with coordinate components and Euclidean norm taken in $z$, satisfy
$$|v_s|\le L v^0,\qquad |v^i|\le L v^0,\qquad v^0\ge L^{-1}|v|_{\mathrm e}>0.$$
In particular these bounds hold throughout any relatively compact $U_0\Subset U'$ whose closure is contained in $P$, equivalently whose time gradient is past timelike on its entire closure. Timelikeness merely on $U_0$ gives local bounds at each point and uniform bounds on each compact subset of $U_0$; it does not alone give a uniform bound on all of $U_0$.

No additional choice is used to select the pointwise linear bases or compact cone constants. Countable and Dependent Choice are explicitly required only for the general absolutely continuous curve clause (c), through its actual calculus suppliers.

after.claim: (The narrowing metric.) Fix the adapted chart $(U_0,x)$ and the constant $K$ of [L1]. Define $g_\varepsilon$ on $U_0$ with $\varepsilon:=3K^2$. For every $q\in U_0$ and every nonzero future $g$-causal $v\in T_qM$ one has $(v^0)^2>0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2\le3K^2(v^0)^2$, so $$g_\varepsilon(v,v)=-(1+\varepsilon)(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2\le(3K^2-1-\varepsilon)(v^0)^2=-(v^0)^2<0,$$ and $v^0>0$: thus $v$ is future $g_\varepsilon$-timelike. Consequently every future $g$-causal curve whose velocity is nonzero almost everywhere is a future $g_\varepsilon$-timelike curve, and the same holds on every subinterval on which the velocity is nonzero almost everywhere.

(The diamonds.) Choose numbers $\delta_k>0$ with $\delta_k\downarrow0$ so small that the points $r_k:=x^{-1}(-\delta_k,0)$ and $q_k:=x^{-1}(\delta_k,0)$, $k\ge1$, and the coordinate segments joining them lie in $U_0$; the $x^0$-axis is an integral curve of the future timelike field $\partial_0$ with $g_\varepsilon(\partial_0,\partial_0)=-(1+\varepsilon)<0$, so the segment from $r_k$ to $q_k$ is a future $g_\varepsilon$-timelike curve and $q_k\in I^+_\varepsilon(r_k)$. Define $V_k:=I^+_\varepsilon(r_k)\cap I^-_\varepsilon(q_k)$, an open subset of $U_0$ containing $p$. Because $r_k\ll_\varepsilon r_{k+1}$ and $q_{k+1}\ll_\varepsilon q_k$, transitivity gives $V_{k+1}\subseteq V_k$. Moreover $\{V_k\}$ is a local basis at $p$: for every $z\in V_k$ the $g_\varepsilon$-causal curves from $r_k$ to $z$ and from $z$ to $q_k$ have strictly increasing $x^0$-coordinate and satisfy $|dx^i|\le\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,dx^0$ along their velocities, so $|x^0(z)|<\delta_k$ and $|x^i(z)|\le\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\cdot2\delta_k$; hence $V_k\subseteq x^{-1}(B_{C\delta_k})$ with $C:=2\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}+1$, and $V_k\subseteq O$ for every open $O\ni p$ once $C\delta_k$ is below the radius of a coordinate ball in $O$ by [L5].

(The witnesses.) For each $k\ge1$ apply the failure hypothesis to the open set $V_k$ with $p\in V_k\subseteq U$: there are a future causal curve $\sigma_k$ and parameters $s_k<t_k$ in its domain with $\sigma_k(s_k),\sigma_k(t_k)\in V_k$ and $\sigma_k([s_k,t_k])\not\subseteq V_k$. Replace $\sigma_k$ by the reparametrized restriction $\sigma_k\circ\varphi_k$ on $[0,1]$, where $\varphi_k:[0,1]\to[s_k,t_k]$ is the increasing affine parametrization; then $\sigma_k(0),\sigma_k(1)\in V_k$ and $\sigma_k([0,1])\not\subseteq V_k$.

(Relative causal convexity.) $V_{k+1}$ is causally convex in $V_k$: if $\eta:[0,1]\to V_k$ is a future $g$-causal curve with $\eta(0),\eta(1)\in V_{k+1}$, then $\eta([0,1])\subseteq V_{k+1}$.
